chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Leaving Vinson's package tour over money
summary: Vinson toured with the Ink Spots and Dinah Washington but got into drinking and gambling and mishandled the money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, that is another story. There's something I was going to ask you about -- something that had to do with the big bands, but it's gone out of my head right now. Anyway, so we're getting a little sidetracked, because how long did you stay with Cleanhead?
I stayed with Cleanhead about maybe eight months, maybe.
Then comes Hines. How did that happen?
After Cleanhead?
I mean, did Earl take you away from Cleanhead, or what?
No. No, I'd left Cleanhead's band. I left Cleanhead in St. Louis.
Why? Were the bookings not too good?
Well, the bookings were all right, in a way. But it was money reasons, one of those things.
Yeah, yeah. Well, the management was not -- that wasn't a good office, was it? Did Tim Gale travel with you at all?
No.
Oh.
No. He had -- Eddie Vinson, I think he had one of the best breaks for a young musician I want to
know, because when the band went out, we had the InksPots with us.
Oh.
The InksPots with us, Dinah Washington and all like that.
You had a package.
We had a package. Moke and Poke, all those. That went out with Eddie Vinson.
Well, how come you couldn't get your money out of who? Out of Cleanhead or --
Well, later on things got kind of bad because he was drinking.
Yeah, I was going to ask you, yeah.
And he was messing up with the money. When he'd get drunk he was gambling a lot.
